assessment: Section 21 is a substantial and candid inventory, not a complete preservation argument. It correctly leaves OPEN the main restrictions and changes. Correct its original-v5 versus repaired-v6 baseline, excluded-output mode reporting, read/report history, new byte-read/attribute/SEEK compatibility failures, D3 causation, D8 causation/deadlines and copy/growth-cap claims. Every incompatible accepted case remains an engineering obligation; review grants no exception.

catalogue.reason: Remove pre-custody chmod. Correct the residual claim that no uncreated source object is mutated: reads can update atime.
Withdraw foreign-owner admission refusal; selecting a non-preserving copy route does not discharge preservation.
Withdraw effective-write-bit admission refusal; copied metadata and subsequent behavior still need the original guarantee.
Withdraw set-ID output refusal. Excluded output file modes are checked transiently, not recorded in the original files map.
Withdraw cross-device directory refusal. Any copy must preserve the accepted filesystem cases rather than assume all support COPY.
Withdraw parent-stage refusal for these scans in favor of route selection. The copy-route non-success cases remain new.
Retracting the false no-changes claim is correct; no acceptance follows.
Different credentials can remove previously accepted access and signaling behavior. An engineering run cannot establish universal equivalence.
Relocated environment and non-writable HOME alter previously available paths and writes.
NNP and seccomp refuse previously permitted modes, io_uring and openat2 behavior; retaining the command allowlist does not preserve accepted actions.
Manager filters, unit masking, no PAM and no bus restrict previously available behavior; H2/BUS are compatibility obligations, not exceptions.
Different manager, slice and delegated-controller context changes scope and unit observations.
Reduced home visibility changes accepted path access in either exposure option.
Enforced frame-writer custody is required. Blanket target write denial also rejects temporary changes that the original could accept after restoration; do not infer preservation from the boundary.
Pre-created non-replaceable roots change target root lifecycle. ROOTS must not become a new input/fixture restriction.
Different credentials remove original writes; the target-write residual is an inventory, not confinement or permission to change accepted cases.
Fixed-size/noexec/cross-filesystem images cannot replace original successful capacity or native execution controls; a genuinely compatible frame remains required.

New inodes, owners, metadata omissions, mounts and disconnected late writes are real observable behavior changes. Bytes/name equivalence and finite compatibility runs cannot discharge exact preservation.
The frame causes an inode atime update on a source that may be outside T. A read label and stat_key exclusion provide no V5-B02 exception.
Retained evidence can be a design cost within T; it must be fully budgeted and cannot silently remove required backup/restore scope.
W-owned parent/root exchange is conditionally confined, but changes P_adm parent metadata after M8. Reconcile admission timing and partition invariants without deleting checks.
Extra work is a custody cost; new timeout refusals of previously successful valid operations are not preservation.
Protecting record and tree access is a custody design choice; relocated access/export cannot silently replace any required producer or source custody.
These are operator-owned setup choices with exact prestate/rollback, not authority granted by this review and not a new approval gate.
Refusal on failed/unknown enforced custody is appropriate; rejecting an originally accepted leftover or benign prior frame participant is a new gate and cannot close preservation.
R/GATE readability differs from sicarii. Also copying needs successful byte reads whereas the original excluded-file walk only opens and stats.

The observed-size data ceiling and longer copy stability window add refusals. Stable originals may also hit new source-read, SEEK_DATA/HOLE, metadata, allocation or exchange failures; not all require continuing writers.
Additional real copy/evidence cost must enter Gate 0 and cannot lower reserve. Establishing capacity may defer work. This does not authorize D3's new accepted-output growth cap.

Global uid/manager/lease conditions exceed original terminal ownership. Even ended participants and a closed foreign-owned file yield UNKNOWN. Preserve the original release obligation without durability gates.
No success credit for an unfinal stream is sound, but an externally retained writable stream is a new success restriction. No archival/durability hold may block known-terminal release.

Final leaf and custody revalidation follows V5-B01. It is still additional to original parent-child directory joins; the claim that any failure proves a K7 premise failed depends on the missing common-state proof.

Malformed messages and unavailable custody fail closed. New deadlines, record/transport failures and forced non-success after recovery are real new outcomes for valid original cases; target-driven copy/observation volume can contribute.

Umask, core limit, scope memory/swap values, allowlist and original window rules are retained at specification level. Isolate frame-v6's required final-pass repair from the original S5 baseline and do not call extended D5 an unchanged gate.
